slothdb runs SQL over local files from R. It compiles the experimental
[SlothDB](https://github.com/SouravRoy-ETL/slothdb) engine into the package
and puts a DBI driver on top, so there is no server, no system library and
no download. This page connects, queries one CSV file, and shows how the
package handles types, failures and writing.

```{r setup}
library(DBI)
library(slothdb)

cars <- tempfile(fileext = ".csv")
write.csv(mtcars, cars, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Connect and query a file

`slothdb()` is a DBI driver, used the way `duckdb::duckdb()` is: code moves
between the two by changing the first argument of `dbConnect()`. The engine
reads files through SQL table functions, so there is no import step.

```{r}
con <- dbConnect(slothdb(), dbdir = ":memory:")

dbGetQuery(con, paste0(
  "SELECT cyl, count(*) AS n, avg(mpg) AS mpg ",
  "FROM read_csv(", dbQuoteString(con, cars), ") GROUP BY cyl ORDER BY cyl"
))

# Open: what slothdb_read() returns and whether it takes reader options (Q12)
slothdb_read(con, cars)
```

## Values arrive as R types, or not at all

Every engine type maps to one R type, and a value that would lose
information is an error instead of a rounded number. A 64-bit integer is a
double by default; beyond 2^53 you choose a wider type when connecting.

```{r}
dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT DATE '2026-11-17' AS day, 42::BIGINT AS n")

dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT 9007199254740993::BIGINT AS n")
# a slothdb_type_error

con64 <- dbConnect(slothdb(), bigint = "integer64")
dbGetQuery(con64, "SELECT 9007199254740993::BIGINT AS n")
dbDisconnect(con64)
```

## Failures are classed conditions

The engine never takes the R session down: its errors come back as
conditions that inherit from `slothdb_error`, so a caller can tell a bad
query from a missing feature. SlothDB has no prepared statements, so
parameters are refused in v0.1.0.

```{r}
tryCatch(
  dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT no_such_column FROM read_csv('missing.csv')"),
  slothdb_sql_error = function(e) conditionMessage(e)
)

dbGetQuery(con, "SELECT ? AS x", params = list(1))
# a slothdb_unsupported error
```

## Write tables and keep them

Data frames are written through the engine's appender, and a file database
persists them. A database file is tied to the package version that wrote
it.

```{r}
dbWriteTable(con, "cars", mtcars)
dbAppendTable(con, "cars", mtcars[1:3, ])

dbBegin(con)
dbExecute(con, "DELETE FROM cars WHERE cyl = 8")
dbRollback(con)

dbListTables(con)
dbDisconnect(con, shutdown = TRUE)
```

## Where next

The [reference index](https://pedrobtz.github.io/slothdb/reference/) lists
every function. `slothdb_info()` reports the engine commit, the patches
applied and the thread count.
